en.tagline: An adults-only beachfront boutique hotel on Kabalana Beach, Ahangama, Sri Lanka.
en.closing: See live dates on our own booking page. If you have a question first, call or email us.

copyBlocks.heading: Pause, take a deep breath & exhale. You are home.
copyBlocks.body:
Designed to feel like an exclusive private beach house with the amenities of an intimate boutique hotel. Your relaxation starts as you kick off your shoes and slip through the hidden door in the wide wooden façade.

Inside, you will catch the first glimpses of our star attraction, The Indian Ocean, magnificent and omnipresent.

Whether you are enjoying the sunshine on the expansive lawns, lounging all day around our abundant, airy indoor living spaces or cooling off in our air-conditioned media room, the sea is always your view.

Dipping your feet in the azure waters of our swimming pool, you will soon be hypnotised by the allure of the white tipped surf breaks just a few meters ahead.

copyBlocks.heading: Why Sandhya
copyBlocks.body:
Sandhya, in Sanskrit संध्य, means “twilight.” It is that magical moment between light and dark.

Come evening, as temperature cools and the sun begins to set over the majestic Indian Ocean, the beauty of twilight is undeniable with its ethereal glow of orange, pink and blue hues painting the cotton candy-clouded sky.

copyBlocks.heading: Casual Luxe
copyBlocks.body:
Casual Luxe is at the heart of our ethos at The Sandhya. We prioritise understated design, thoughtful form and practical function above conspicuous bling and glitter.

Our property’s furnishings are inspired by mid-century aesthetics and embellished with mod-chinoiserie decor. Our Singaporean owner’s discerning vision has been brought to life by the local designers and craftsmen he worked with across Sri Lanka.

Wallpaper* describes The Sandhya as “a clean-lined boutique hotel with Scandinavian design sensibilities.”

We opened in 2017 and renovated in 2023.

Our service is warm, kind, attentive yet informal. Ask for your heart’s desire or simply be left alone when seeking that self-restoration. Just feel at home and allow us to look after you.

We have blended the best of the worlds that we live in. We are not international. We are not local. We are simply The Sandhya.

copyBlocks.heading: Looking after the place
copyBlocks.body: We support the local community and our environment, with a zero-food waste menu, a ban on single-use plastic, water recycling and a care programme for our beach turtles. We strive for sustainable tourism.

copyBlocks.heading: The rooms
copyBlocks.body:
Our 9 spacious rooms have unobstructed sweeping views of the beach and beyond to the endless ocean, each with its own private balcony or exclusive patio area.

We have included thoughtful touches from evening lavender scents to high pressure rain showers so you are assured of a restorative stay in any one of our room types.

Every room has a plush pillow-top mattress with 500 thread count linen, a shower big enough for two, Spa Ceylon amenities, bathrobes and slippers. Each one also has central air conditioning and a ceiling fan, a desk, universal sockets, a hairdryer and a Bluetooth speaker. High speed WiFi too, with newspapers and magazines from around the world on PressReader.

In the Studio King, a triple occupancy can be arranged (subject to availability) with a supplement.

Nightly rates are on our booking page, for the dates you choose.

copyBlocks.heading: The Dining Room
copyBlocks.body:
Elevated Comfort Food was the brief for our visiting menu designer, Chef Christophe DuBois. Working closely with our owner, a self-confessed “easy foodie”, the team conjured a delectable array of dishes inspired from a global set-list of food heaven highlights.

We truly believe some of the island’s best qualities may be expressed through our food. Our signature Sri Lankan rice & curry, our zesty DIY poke bowls and our localized “Tom Yum” style noodles with fresh Ceylon prawns explore the diversity of the local produce available. Or go directly to a finger licking array of delicious homemade desserts.

Our breads, pastas, sauces, infused mayonnaise, stocks, spice blends, jams are made in-house and the menus subtly evolve with the seasons.

If you don’t find what you crave, simply ask our team to prepare what your tummy desires. Dishes catering to vegetarian, vegan, keto and other dietary lifestyles are available.

A continental breakfast for two adults is included in your stay.

copyBlocks.heading: Exclusive Use
copyBlocks.body:
Our home at The Sandhya can be your very own private beach house with an Exclusive Use booking. Our position on Kabalana Beach, in a secluded nook, lends itself to an intimate wedding party, birthday celebration, family reunion, wellness/fitness retreat or simply to celebrate life.

With the beach as your blank canvas and with our delightful staff at your service, we offer a private setting for your special occasion.

copyBlocks.heading: Kabalana and around
copyBlocks.body:
Just by the buzzing and eclectic town of Ahangama, Kabalana Beach has come into its own in recent years with surfers, families, and digital nomads alike. Pristine sand and stunning sunsets have nurtured a laid-back scene where surf lovers, beach bunnies, serial retreat hunters and quiet couples coexist with welcoming locals.

Centuries old Galle Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is just 25 minutes away. While away a whole day browsing through an eclectic array of boutiques, stopping for well-earned sips and bites from an ever-growing cafe and restaurant scene.

The nearby beaches of Midigama, Weligama, Mirissa, Madiha and Hiriketiya Bay have surf points and whale-watching boat rides. You will find plenty of places to eat there too. Our own town Ahangama has grown into a foodies’ haven with a diverse selection of high-quality eateries and night spots.

Yala and Udwalawe National Parks, Singharaja Forest and awe-inspiring waterfalls are within manageable day trips from The Sandhya. Depart your room in the crisp early morning and be back in time for a late lunch or cocktail.

Ahangama train station is 1.4 km from us.

testimonials.quote: It’s a beautiful place and a well maintained clean stay. The staff is very supportive. The Sandhya is situated near one of the best locations which is facing stunning kabalana beach .the pool omg !!! That was awesome. It’s a long crystal clean relaxing pool with the stunning view of the ocean . Food is delicious and a well curated menu. Rooms are beautiful and very comfortable. Overall we loved the stay and everything in it . It’s a must go boutique hotel in ahangama .
testimonials.author: Guest User

testimonials.quote: A great stay, absolutely gorgeous hotel - perfect, friendly and attentive service, small hotel so felt very safe, familiar and luxurious. Delicious food, excellent location to get to Ahangama by 5min TukTuk and be directly on a wide sandy and long (enough) beach with lots of surfers, without the actual beach being packed full of people so was calm but bustling. Would highly recommend.

image.alt: From a white bed in a pale room, floor-to-ceiling glass doors stand between grey curtains. Through them, one palm on the centre line, a sandy beach and a green-blue sea. A round table, chairs with woven seats and a red-shaded lamp stand to the left of the bed.
Tall slatted teak doors standing open under a concrete canopy, with three low steps in front. Inside, a stair and a wall of glass.

From inside a room, a wall of glass in black frames. Beyond it a terrace of patterned tile with a metal lounge chair, a pool, a green lawn, two tall palms and the sea. A red-shaded lamp and a small round table stand by the curtain on the left.
A blue patterned plate of wide pasta with herbs and a red crab shell on top, on a wooden table beside a dark napkin and cutlery.
Seen from above, a round wooden table laid with small plates and bowls, between two slatted wooden seats on a stone floor.
A blue and white bowl of salad with halved boiled eggs, avocado and tomato on a woven placemat with gold cutlery.
Noodles with prawns and green beans in a patterned bowl on a wooden table, with chopsticks and a small patterned bowl.

A double-height lounge. A stair climbs the pale wall on a fan of thin steel rods, low sun lies across the floor, wooden armchairs and a grey sofa face a wall of glass, and through it a long blue pool, parasols and the sea.
Close on a dark wooden chair frame curving over a woven paper-cord seat.
Close on a wooden hoop chair strung with white cord, with a pale cushion tied into it.
Close on a pale wooden armrest over a basket-woven seat back.
The corner of a teak desk with a dark inlaid panel.
The arm of a blue upholstered armchair with a small wooden cap, on a pale stone floor.
A black metal lounge chair and footstool with dark wooden slats on a black and white patterned tile floor.
Black and white: a smiling staff member in a white shirt and glasses reading a tablet by the stair.
Black and white: a staff member in a white polo shirt smoothing a bed beside a round lamp.
Black and white: a staff member in a white shirt setting a cup on a low table from a tray.
Looking along a raked sandy beach from the edge of a green lawn, with a dark stone bowl and a slate sign bearing the hotel's logo in the foreground and two people far off by the water.
The hotel's own drawn map of the south-west coast of Sri Lanka: the road from the airport and Colombo down past Galle to The Sandhya, drawn as a small building on the sea, with Weligama beyond it.
The long two-storey block with its decks and glass from the lawn: tall palms, tables under white parasols, a line of loungers beside the pool and the sea at the far right.
The hotel's two-storey concrete frame at blue hour, each room's curtains lit gold against a deep blue sky.
A sunset over the sea, gold light breaking through dark clouds onto wet sand, with palms and a roof in silhouette on the right.
